sci-repo-y10-sby-2020-evolution-wip-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Evolution general source draft —SafetyBay2020 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-sby-2020-evolution-wip-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: The dog breeds we have today were developed through
questions.explanation: Artificial selection by people developed dog breeds.

questions.prompt: Characteristics of an organism that have the same basic structure are
questions.explanation: Homologous features share an underlying inherited structural origin;functions may differ.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the ship that took Charles Darwin around the world?
questions.explanation: HMSBeagle.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct term for the following definition. “Genetic change in the characteristics of a species over many generations, resulting in the formation of new species.”
questions.explanation: Evolution:heritable change in populations over generations;speciation may result but is not required for every evolutionary change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is usually an outcome (result) of natural selection?
options: A species slowly becomes better adapted to its environment.
Variations will appear in the offspring (babies).
Mutations slowly disappear over time, because they are harmful.
A species slowly becomes less adapted to its environment.
questions.explanation: A is the best listed outcome under stable selection conditions;variation and mutation do not arise because organisms need them.

questions.prompt: According to Darwin’s theory of natural selection, individuals who survive are the ones best adapted for their environment. Their survival is due to the?
options: Possession of inherited adaptations that maximise fitness.
questions.explanation: Inherited traits affecting relative reproductive success are central;being strongest/fastest is not a universal measure of fitness.

questions.prompt: A population of bacteria is treated with hand sanitizer. Because of genetic variation in the population, what is a possible outcome?
options: All of the bacteria are already resistant.
They will get better at obtaining a food source.
Some may be resistant and survive.
questions.explanation: Some pre-existing resistant variants may survive and reproduce;the sanitiser does not intentionally create the needed variation.

questions.prompt: Charles Darwin was famous for
options: suggesting natural selection was the mechanism of evolution.
writing a book called ‘The Origin of Species’ that showed how natural selection resulted from evolution.
inventing the term artificial selection and proposing that it caused evolution.
questions.explanation: B:natural selection is an important mechanism of evolution.

sci-repo-y8-sby-2018-microscopes-mc-1.title: Year 8 Science — Microscopes and cells —SafetyBay2018 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y8-sby-2018-microscopes-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: The smallest unit of life is..
questions.explanation: A cell is the smallest independently living structural unit in the intended cellular-life model.

questions.prompt: The magnification of the microscope tells you
options: how big the lenses in the microscope are
how much smaller the image is than the real object
how much bigger the image is than the real object
how much light is passing through the object
questions.explanation: Magnification is image size divided by actual object size.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the smallest unit of length?
questions.explanation: Micrometres are smallest among the listed units.

questions.prompt: A micrometre (µm) is:
questions.explanation: One micrometre(µm)=0.001 millimetre. The original Word Symbol-font µ is retained as Unicode.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure allows substances to enter and leave the cell?
questions.explanation: Cell membrane regulates entry and exit.

questions.prompt: The main benefit of staining is…
options: Increasing the size of cells, making them easier to see
Slows down movement of living cells, making them easier to see
Improves the contrast, making the cell and its features stand out more
Improve the colour, making it more interesting
questions.explanation: Staining improves contrast between structures.

questions.prompt: When carrying a microscope, what is the safest part to hold?
questions.explanation: Hold the arm securely with one hand and support the base with the other;arm is the best listed part.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a part of animal cells?
questions.explanation: Animal cells do not have a cell wall.

questions.prompt: What is the definition of a unicellular organism?
options: more than one cell living thing
questions.explanation: A unicellular organism consists of a single cell.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the cell wall in plant cells?
options: allow nutrients in and out of the cell
hold the organelles of the cell
provide structure and support to the cell
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall provides mechanical support and shape.

questions.prompt: What does a plant cell have that an animal cell does not?
questions.explanation: Chloroplast is the best listed plant-specific feature in the typical photosynthetic plant-cell comparison;not every plant cell has one.

questions.prompt: Mitochondria, ribosomes, lysosomes and endoplasmic reticulum are  examples of
questions.explanation: They are organelles.

sci-repo-y8-aran-2013-physend-mc-1.title: Year 8 Science — Energy end-of-topic test —Aranmore2013 (original source MC)

questions.prompt: 1 Energy is measured using a unit called the:
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules.

questions.prompt: 2 Select which of the following require energy to happen.
options: a leaf falling from a tree
questions.explanation: Each situation involves an energy transfer or transformation.

questions.prompt: 3 The energy of a moving object is called:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy.

questions.prompt: 4 Jordan watches a music video clip on his iPhone. Choose the best description of the  energy transformations that are happening.
options: electrical energy   → sound energy + light energy + heat energy
electrical energy   → sound energy + light energy
sound energy + light energy + heat energy  →   electrical energy
sound energy + light energy  →   electrical energy
questions.explanation: A:electrical input becomes light,sound and thermal energy.

questions.prompt: 5 A particular electric knife is 40% efficient. If 100 J of energy is supplied to the knife how  many joules are then transformed into kinetic energy ?
questions.explanation: 40%of100J=40J useful kinetic output.

questions.prompt: 6 The number of stars found on an Energy Rating Label indicate:
options: the energy efficiency of an appliance.
how much energy the appliance will require to operate.
how much effort needs to be taken to maintain the appliance.
how easy the appliance is to clean.
questions.explanation: Stars communicate comparative energy efficiency within the label’s appliance class.

questions.prompt: 7 Select which of the following contains elastic potential energy.
options: a stretched bow about to fire an arrow
questions.explanation: The stretched bow has elastic potential energy.

questions.prompt: 8 Select which device transforms chemical energy into kinetic energy.
questions.explanation: Battery-operated car converts chemical energy via electrical energy to motion.

questions.prompt: 9 Heat flows from areas of:
options: higher temperature to those of lower temperature.
lower temperature to those of higher temperature.
questions.explanation: Net spontaneous heat transfer is from hotter to colder regions.

questions.prompt: 10 Select the correct energy flow diagram showing energy changes that occur when operating a  battery-operated fire truck that moves and sounds a siren.
options: electrical energy  →  chemical energy + sound energy
electrical energy  →  heat + elastic potential energy
chemical energy  →   kinetic energy + sound + heat
questions.explanation: Chemical input→kinetic,sound and thermal outputs.

questions.prompt: 11 If a food processor is 25% efficient, then for every 10 kJ input, its useful energy output is:
12 The efficiency of the  Spinners washing machine is 40%, Sparkles washing machine is 35% and the Sprinkles washing machine is 52%, The machines listed from most to least efficient are:
questions.explanation: 52%Sprinkles,40%Spinners,35%Sparkles.

questions.prompt: 17 Which of the following factors affect the amount of kinetic energy possessed by an object?

sci-repo-y8-aran-2015-energy-mc-1.title: Year 8 Science — Energy source test —Aranmore2015 (original source MC)
sci-repo-y8-aran-2015-energy-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Q1. Kate accidentally drops a chocolate cake on the floor. Select the most likely sequence of energy transformations that occur:
options: Heat energy → gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → sound energy
Gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → sound energy →heat energy
Kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy → heat energy → sound energy
Sound energy → kinetic energy → heat energy → gravitational potential energy
questions.explanation: B is closest:gravitational potential becomes kinetic,then dissipates into sound/thermal energy on impact;outputs are not necessarily strictly sequential.

questions.prompt: Q2. Energy is measured using the unit?
questions.explanation: Joules.

questions.prompt: Q3. Stored energy is called?
questions.explanation: Potential energy.

questions.prompt: Q5. When energy is passed from one object to another we call this a?
questions.explanation: Energy transfer.

questions.prompt: Q6. The law of energy conservation is;
options: That energy can never be created or destroyed, it just transfers from one form to another.
That energy can be created and destroyed.
That energy is only released when you feel heat.
That if something is not moving it does not have energy.
questions.explanation: A:energy is conserved and changes form/transfers between systems.

questions.prompt: Q8. An energy rating label found on appliances shows its energy efficiency by what symbol?
questions.explanation: Stars on the appliance energy-rating label.

questions.prompt: Q9. Reducing the amount of energy we use reduces the amount of ___________ ______ put into the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Energy use linked to fossil-fuel combustion can produce greenhouse gases;the amount depends on the energy source.

questions.prompt: Q10. The National House Energy Rating Scheme suggests you take steps to make your house more energy efficient and therefore cheaper to run, heat and cool. Which of the following would they disapprove of?
options: Insulation in walls, roof and floor
6 Star reverse cycle air conditioning system
questions.explanation: Incandescent bulbs typically use more electricity for equivalent light than efficient alternatives;source item is historical energy-efficiency guidance.
